headline: The quiet stretch broke with a genuinely brisk tempo effort — the fastest-paced run in weeks, with real time above threshold. Legs are primed, not dulled. Now let the taper reassert itself.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The three-day running gap ended with a session that was anything but easy — a sustained tempo with meaningful time in the upper zones, the sharpest quality run of this wind-down. That's a useful sign the taper hasn't gone flat: the legs answered a hard ask cleanly at a fast pace. Set against it, strength has stayed in its low-intensity functional groove, exactly the durability-holding cadence you want with the crossing close. Steps remain high on active days, keeping background load ticking over even as structured running thins. The one signal pulling the other way is the strain reading sitting at floor, flagging "detraining" — but that's a rolling-average artefact of a light stretch, not a fitness statement, and today's tempo directly contradicts it. Recovery-wise sleep is still erratic, worth simple awareness as logistics ramp, not a lever to pull.
sections.trends: The recent four-week block sits well above the prior one, and the year-to-date comparison against last year is a different order of magnitude entirely — this has been a real building year, not a maintenance one. The current thinning of volume reads clearly as a deliberate pre-event wind-down layered on top of a genuine base, not a stall. Given the crossing is the near-term anchor, the shape makes sense: build through spring and early summer, then ease into the departure window while keeping the engine warm.
sections.threshold: The threshold figure remains the early-July benchmark with no full 30-day baseline yet, so treat it as a reference point rather than a live trend. What today adds is corroboration: a fast tempo pace held with a controlled max tells you the aerobic-to-threshold machinery is intact and responsive. Nothing here suggests the taper has cost you sharpness — if anything, the opposite.
sections.zones: Today's session is a real departure from the string of low, controlled easy runs that defined the last two weeks — a genuine tempo with substantial time in Z3 and a solid block in Z4, not a steady cruise that happens to average high. That's a legitimate primer effort and appropriate as a single sharpening touch before a long slow event; you don't want a diet of these now, but one is exactly the kind of stimulus that keeps the legs from going stale. The surrounding runs stayed properly polarised in Z1–Z2, so the block's overall distribution remains sound.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions continue to sit low and aerobic, consistent with the functional-fitness character rather than heavy loading — no drift upward, which is what you want with running light. The most recent strength work didn't log HR, so there's less to read there, but the pattern across the block is stable and unremarkable in the good sense.
sections.calendar: The rhythm here is a clear taper signature: running frequency has dropped while strength held its cadence, then a single quality run punctuating the quiet. That's a controlled wind-down, not an erratic one — the gaps are chosen, and the return today was purposeful rather than a random resumption. Consistency over the longer run of weeks remains the real story underneath.
sections.personal_bests: None of the standing PBs are the target of this phase — the focus is a self-supported multi-day crossing, a durability event, not a time trial. Today's tempo pace, while sharp for this block, sits comfortably off the 5K and 10K bests set last late-summer, and chasing those isn't the point right now. Worth noting only that the underlying speed clearly hasn't evaporated during the base build.

watch_items: Watch that the easy runs, when they resume, settle back into their low band — today's tempo was a deliberate one-off, not a new baseline for the wind-down.
Watch for any residual fatigue or soreness in the next day or two after today's harder effort, since it's the highest-intensity session in a fortnight.
Watch that strength holds its low-intensity cadence into departure rather than creeping up as the main durability input.
Watch recovery consistency as pre-event logistics build — sleep remains erratic and worth noting, not acting on.
